summary: The scrub map's `Wong Tai Sin` guard now tolerates a line break — the first real rewrite corrupted the one live occurrence into `Walsh\n        Tai Sin` because the source comment wraps between the two words.
details: `regex:\bWalsh\b(?! Tai Sin)` matched a single literal space, and `nora/agent/tools.py` wraps the temple's name across two lines. `(?!\s+Tai Sin)` fixes it.

No identifier leaked: the failure was in the other direction, scrubbing real geography to hide a name the full-name rules had already removed — exactly what the deliberate-keeps list exists to prevent.

Found by diffing the published pack against the original for each of the three keeps rather than by trusting the map: `May Chan` (57 occurrences) and `Pok Fu Lam` (1) were checked the same way and are intact.
limitations: Lookbehind guards cannot be made whitespace-tolerant the same way — Python requires them to be fixed-width — so `(?<!Pok Fu )` would still miss a line break. It holds today because the only `Pok Fu Lam` in the tree is inline; a future wrapped one would need a different rule shape.
